mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL stays elevated while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain deeply depressed, at-home substitution dominates and discretionary shopping stays suppressed. Over the next four weeks, RETAIL_REC should remain lower than the prior four-week average unless outside-home activity rebounds first.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week mean even though RESIDENTIAL remains above 25% and WORKPLACES stays below -70% through the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp weekly drop in TRANSIT below the prior week signals tighter movement restrictions or collapsing commuting access. That shock should reduce retail trips within one to two weeks and keep RETAIL_REC below the recent four-week mean until transit stabilizes.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -85% and remains there for 2 consecutive weekly means
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 14 days after TRANSIT crosses below -85% and stays there for two weekly means.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM is less negative than RETAIL_REC while PARKS and RESIDENTIAL stay weakly supportive of non-work trips, households are concentrating on essentials rather than discretionary shopping. This should keep RETAIL_REC soft over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC turns higher over the next 14 days while GROCERY_PHARM remains less depressed than RETAIL_REC and PARKS does not recover.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS begin to recover from very depressed levels, outdoor recreation substitutes for indoor retail visits and keeps retail-and-recreation mobility from rebounding as fast as other movement. A sustained park rebound should therefore reduce RETAIL_REC relative to the previous four weeks over a four-week horizon.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 15 points from its recent weekly mean
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days despite PARKS rising by 15 points or more from the recent weekly mean.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain jointly suppressed, commuting-linked shopping demand cannot recover even when grocery trips stabilize. The combined weakness should keep RETAIL_REC below the trailing four-week average for the next month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week mean over the next 28 days while WORKPLACES stays below -70% and TRANSIT stays below -80%.

mechanism_narrative: A short-run improvement in GROCERY_PHARM relative to RETAIL_REC indicates that foot traffic is shifting toward essential errands before discretionary shopping returns. That pattern should keep RETAIL_REC lower over the next week, especially if WORKPLACES is still deeply negative.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above -70% after being at or below -75% in the prior week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases within 7 days after GROCERY_PHARM improves above -70% and WORKPLACES remains below -75%.

mechanism_narrative: As RESIDENTIAL mobility normalizes from its elevated lockdown level, some time spent at home is reallocated to local discretionary trips, lifting RETAIL_REC over a one-week to two-week horizon. This effect should appear only if residence time stops rising.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stops increasing and falls at least 2 points from the prior weekly mean
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within 7 days after RESIDENTIAL falls by at least 2 points from its prior weekly mean.

mechanism_narrative: When all six mobility series remain near their recent troughs, the area is in a persistent suppression regime where discretionary retail recovery lags behind every other category. A flat-lining pattern across WORKPLACES, TRANSIT, and RESIDENTIAL should therefore predict further weakness in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises for four consecutive weeks even though TRANSIT, WORKPLACES, and RESIDENTIAL all stay within 3 points of their current weekly means.
